t: Shaka turned a small chiefdom into the strongest state in southeastern Africa between 1816 and 1828.
Its power rested on age-regiments (amabutho) of young men bound to the king and on royal control of cattle.
The Zulu routed a British force at Isandlwana in 1879 but were defeated at Ulundi, and Britain annexed Zululand in 1887.
dyk: Zulu regiments could marry only with the king’s permission, often granted when the men were in their late thirties, giving the king control over new households.
ev: Shaka seizes leadership of the Zulu chiefdom with Mthethwa support
Shaka defeats the Ndwandwe at the Mhlatuze river
Shaka is assassinated at Dukuza by his half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana
Boer forces defeat Dingane’s army at the Battle of Blood River
Cetshwayo defeats his brother Mbuyazi at the Battle of Ndondakusuka
The Zulu win at Isandlwana but are defeated at Ulundi
Cetshwayo is restored to part of Zululand; civil war follows
Britain annexes Zululand as a British colony

f.capital: KwaBulawayo; later Dukuza, uMgungundlovu and Ulundi
